Judge, Court Of Small Causes & Member, M.A.C.T, Mayo Hall Unit, Bengaluru (Scch-21) Present: Vijaykumar S. Hiremath., L.Lb., Xvii Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, M.A.C.T., Bengaluru. Dated this the 10th Day of January-2025 M.V.C. No.7183/2022 Petitioner/s: 1. Sri. Channa Krishnappa M. C S/o Chowdappa, Aged about 36 years, Residing at: No.27, Marasandahalli Village, Bylanarasapura Post, Nandagudi Hobli, Hoskote Taluk, Bangalore Rural District. (By Sri. T. Manjunatha, Adv.,) Vs. Respondent/s: 1. M/s Icici Lombard Motor Ins. Co. Ltd., Motor Claims Hub, No.121, The Estate Building, 9th Floor, Dickson Road, Bangalore-560 001. (Policy No.3005/2012217613/00/0000001207 Valid Upto 11.05.2019 to 10.05.2024) (By Sri. S. Maheswara, Adv.) 2. Sri. Muniswamy Gowda S/o Munirajappa. S, Chikkathimmana Gollahalli, Scch-21 2 Mvc No.7183/2022 KembagakaHalli, Nandagudi Hobli, Hoskote Taluk, Bangalore Rural District-562114. (Owner of Motorcycle bearing No.KA- Channa Krishnappa M.C vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160696662/ 1 53-Hb-5993) (Exparte) Date of institution of the : 21.12.2022 petition Nature of the Petition : U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act Date of commencement of : 15.02.2024 recording of the evidence Date on which the Judgment : 10.01.2025 was pronounced Duration of the Petition Year/s Month/s Day/s 02 00 20 Judgment
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 11.10.2022. 2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under: It is the case of the petitioner that on 11.10.2022 at about 08.45 p.m., petitioner was riding a motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA- 08-H-7521 slowly and cautiously by observing the traffic rules proceeding on Chikkanahalli-Chinnadahalli Village, Nandagudi Hobli Hoskote Taluk, Bangalore, at that time the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HB-5993 ridden in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motorcycle of petitioner from behind. Due to which, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries on vital parts of the body. Immediately, he was shifted to Gaurav Hospital wherein he treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, food, transport and other charges. The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 36 years, the petitioner was working at Ninjacart Company and earning Rs.35,000/- per month. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and lost his future income. Respondent No.1 is the insurer of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle. Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest. 3. After service of notice, the respondent No.2 remained absent. Hence, placed exparte. Channa Krishnappa M.C vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160696662/ 2 The respondent No.1 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and also denying the rash and negligent riding of the offending motorcycle. Further, this respondent admitted the issuance of policy to the offending vehicle and policy was inforce as on the date of accident and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy. Further, this respondent seeks protection u/s 147, 149(2), 134(c), 158(6) of M. V. Act. This respondent further submits that, complaint is lodged after the lapse of 01 day and no valid reason is assigned for the delay in lodging the complaint. Further this respondent submits that, the petitioner was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident. The petitioner was not wearing helmet as on the date of accident. He also denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner. The petitioner colluding with the owner and police filed the false case. By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he has got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.27 and also examined Dr. Nagaraj B. N as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.28 and 29 and closed their side. On the other hand, respondent No.1 examined their witnesses as RW.1 to RW.3 and got marked the documents at Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.5.
texts.arguments: 15. In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319. 16. The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses. In support of his plea, he has produced 13 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.10 to the tune of Rs.39,888/-. The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.39,888/- Channa Krishnappa M.C vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160696662/ 5 towards medical expenses. 21. LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID UP PERIOD: The petitioner has produced Ex.P.9 Discharge summaries issued by Gaurav Orthopaedic and Surgical Hospital, Bangalore, it reveals that, the petitioner took treatment from the said hospital from 11.10.2022 to 15.10.2022 and again from 04.03.2023 to 06.03.2023 i.e. for 06 days. Hence, at least 2 months is required to recover from the accidental injuries. It is the further contended that, the injured petitioner was an employee in Ninjacart Company and earning Rs.35,000/- per month, in support of his income he has produced the Appointment letter, Pay slips and bank statement which are marked at Ex.P.11 to Ex.P.26. As per the pay slips produced at Ex.P.12 to Ex.P.25 as well as Bank statement at Ex.P.26 it reveals that, as on the date of accident petitioner having income of Rs.24,034/- per month by way of salary. The accident is of the year is 2022. Hence, the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.24,034/-p.m. as per above decision. Hence, 2 months is to be considered as loss of income. Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.48,068/- under this head. 22. Towards loss of future earning capacity on account of Permanent Physical Disability- The petitioner contended that, he has discontinued his service due to the accident. But documents produced by the petitioner himself at Ex.P.26 clearly shows that, petitioner taken salary from the company even after the accident also. This itself shows that, the petitioner continued in service. This shows that, the petitioner is not suffering from disability. Hence, this tribunal can infer that there is no disability caused to the petitioner and he is not entitle for the compensation under this head. 23. FOOD, CONVEYANCE, NOURISHMENT AND ATTENDANT CHARGES: Further the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took treatment as inpatient in Gaurav Hospital, Bangalore as inpatient from 11.10.2022 to 15.10.2022 and again from 04.03.2023 to 06.03.2023 i.e., 06 days. Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the head of nutritious food and attendant charges. 24. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS: The petitioner was aged about 36 years at the time of accident, he has sustained grievous injuries. It shows that he found difficulty in doing day to day works. He might have suffered lot of pain and loss of amenities and comforts in life. Therefore, considering the age, nature of injuries and percentage of disability, Rs.20,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of future amenities and happiness. 25. TOWARDS FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES : The petitioner has claimed towards future medical expenses. The doctor who has been examined as PW.2 has suggested for removal of the implants and estimate of this surgery will be approximately Rs.60,000/-. 4 Nutritious food and Rs. 30,000/- attendant charges 5 Loss of future amenities and Rs. 20,000/- loss of happiness. learned counsel for petitioner taken defense that, second respondent not digitized his driving license so same is not reflected in the Sarathi-4 website. learned counsel for petitioner suggested that, second respondent was having driving license but you have filed false charge-sheet against the second respondent/accused. But witness denied the said suggestion. Channa Krishnappa M.C vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160696662/ 7 Vinay Prasad, Manager of respondent No.1 company examined as RW.3, wherein he reiterated the contents of the written statement. Though the learned counsel for petitioner cross examined the RW.3 but failed to culled out from the mouth of witness that, at the time of accident respondent No.2 was having Driving License. In Beli Ram Vs. Rajinder Kumar and Another [AIR 2020 SC 4453] wherein the Apex Court observed as under:- "Motor Vehicles Act (59 of 198), S.149 (2)(ao(ii), S.15 - Insurer's liability - Non-renewal of driving licence - Respondent - Claimant employed as driver met with accident while driving truck owned by employer - License not renewed for period of three years and that too in respect of commercial vehicle like truck - employer cannot wash his hands off responsibility of not checking up whether the driver has renewed license - Gross negligence on part of employees as insured in verifying driving license, Insurance Company not liable to pay compensation." U/sec 3 of M. V Act and also meaning and definition of 'Effective driving licence' viz a viz section 3, 4 and 5 of M. V Act, whereby the insurance company has done all its efforts in establishing the fact that there was a fundamental breach of policy condition. If a person drives the vehicle without a driving license or the owner allows the person to drive the vehicle without driving license there is a breach of section 3 of M. V Act which would no doubt make the owner liable for the consequences as per the M. V act and as per the section 181 of M. V Act. 27. Therefore, judgment in MFA No. 22781/2012 C/w MFA No. 22539/2012 (MV) in a case The Divisional Manager, Reliance General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Shri Arjun Datatray Gurav and another, wherein it is held that when there is fundamental breach of the policy condition the legibility fix on the insurance company. Therefore, this being the violation of the policy conditions while considering the liability. 28. Further this court has relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme court of India 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 932 in a case of Balu Krishna Chavan Vs. The Reliance General Insurance Company Ltd. & others wherein held that if the liability of the insurance company is decided and they are held Channa Krishnappa M.C vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160696662/ 8 not to the liable, ordinarily, there shall be no direction to "pay and recover", Further in para No.8 held that hence, the only aspect for out consideration herein, is as to whether in the facts and circumstances of the present case, an order to direct the Insurance Company to "pay and recover", is required to be made. On this aspect, the law is well settled that if the liability of the Insurance Company is decided and they are held not to be liable, ordinarily, there shall be no direction to "pay and recover". As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.
